headline: High: ECC can write shared files and use MCP while Haystack can call MCP/REST, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC can write/read the filesystem, use MCP, and its session files live in shared paths; Haystack can use MCP servers. That creates a plausible default bridge where ECC-authored content can reach Haystack as instructions. The interaction is documented only indirectly, so uncertainty pushes severity up.
conditions: IF both agents are connected to the same MCP server or shared workspace, attacker-controlled text from ECC can reach Haystack.
IF Haystack parses MCP/file content as instructions, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Disable shared MCP endpoints between the agents.
Separate ECC and Haystack workspaces and roots.
Require provenance labels on all cross-agent content.
Add a manual review step before Haystack follows ECC-produced text.
requires-engineering: enforce content-sanitization at the MCP boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, skills, hooks, git history, and security findings, while Haystack can call REST APIs and MCP servers with broad egress. If they share a workspace or MCP channel, ECC-managed data can flow into Haystack outputs or outbound requests. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace by default, so this stays medium.
conditions: IF ECC and Haystack share files or MCP payloads, ECC session data can be exposed to Haystack.
IF Haystack forwards retrieved context to REST/MCP targets, that context can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep agents on separate directories and credentials.
Block Haystack from reading ECC session files.
Restrict Haystack outbound destinations to an allowlist.
Rotate any secrets stored in ECC-managed files.
requires-engineering: add per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC has filesystem write, git-state modification, subprocesses, and allowlisted egress; Haystack has broad network egress and MCP access. Overlapping write and network surfaces can conflict on shared resources even without explicit locking. Because shared mutable targets are not directly documented, uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repo or directory, concurrent writes can clobber state.
IF both agents target the same MCP-backed resource, race conditions can corrupt shared outputs.
mitigations: Run the agents in separate repos or branches.
Serialize writes with a lock file or queue.
Disable concurrent git mutations.
Assign distinct MCP resources per agent.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC produces session summaries, documentation, and security findings; Haystack is a search/RAG agent that can ingest and re-emit retrieved text. That makes it plausible Haystack will treat ECC output as authoritative without verification. The pairwise handoff is inferred, not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Haystack uses ECC-generated summaries as retrieval corpus, errors can propagate downstream.
IF Haystack acts on retrieved text without a verification step, falsehoods can cascade.
mitigations: Require source citations on all ECC-derived claims.
Add a verification prompt before Haystack acts on retrieved facts.
Limit ECC output to summaries with provenance metadata.
Review high-impact outputs manually before execution.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: ECC explicitly touches security findings, git history, and session data, while Haystack only lists anonymous usage statistics. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so a compliance breach is not established. The other agent is cited because the risk is about cross-agent handling, but the evidence is thin.
conditions: IF ECC is configured to process regulated data and Haystack stores it beyond anonymous statistics, a policy mismatch could arise.
IF either agent is deployed under a residency or retention rule not reflected in the profiles, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through the pair.
Document retention and residency settings for both agents.
Review outbound logs for unexpected personal data.
Keep Haystack limited to anonymous or synthetic inputs.
requires-engineering: align compliance controls across both systems.
